exposure: child care arrangements after return home
cohort: Postpartum women over 20 years old, able to speak Mandarin Chinese or Taiwanese, who delivered singleton, live infants at term and resided in a postpartum nursing center in central Taiwan.
finding: The study found prevalence rates of postpartum depressive symptoms were 13% upon admission and 8% before discharge from a postpartum nursing center, with previous abortion experience and postpartum pain identified as risk factors, and having childcare arrangements and 8-11 hours of sleep per day as protective factors.
mod_finding: Postoperative pain after caesarean delivery was identified as a component of postpartum pain, which was a significant risk factor for postpartum depressive symptoms.
cross-section timing: at first week and last week in the postpartum nursing center
